profile.name: Prototype cross-extractor matching and consilience specification
profile.description: Versioned, checksum-bearing specification governing one cross-extractor matching analysis run. Registered as a config_profiles row of kind consilience_policy and linked to its analysis run through analysis_run_profiles.

calibration_status.meaning: Every numeric threshold below is a deterministic demonstration value chosen to exercise algorithm behaviour on synthetic fixtures. None is empirically calibrated, and none should be reported as an optimal or recommended setting.
calibration_status.evidence_basis: synthetic DeepSqueak and MUPET fixtures only; no real paired extractor session has been available
calibration_status.calibration_requires: a genuine paired extractor session plus an independent manually reviewed reference subset

run_pair.ordering: The caller names run_a and run_b. That order is recorded as analysis_run_extraction_inputs.input_role and is the only ordering in the analysis; candidate_pairs.detection_a_id/detection_b_id are ordered by detection_id to satisfy the schema CHECK and carry no run meaning.

candidate_generation.notes: Every pair satisfying the plausibility rule is written, so one-to-many, many-to-one, and many-to-many evidence remains visible rather than being collapsed to a best match.

candidate_scoring.rationale: The schema provides a candidate_score column. Rather than invent a weighted blend with no empirical support, the score is defined to be exactly the temporal intersection-over-union already stored beside it. Its meaning is therefore documented and reproducible, and the four other evidence fields are never collapsed into it.

assignment.topology_source: member counts per side of the ordered run pair
assignment.detection_partition: every detection of either input run belongs to exactly one match group of this analysis run, including unmatched detections in their own single-member group
assignment.display_label_policy: split and merge are display labels relative to the explicitly ordered run pair, never a claim that one extractor is objectively splitting a true event

consensus.principle: A consensus event is a derived grouping. It never replaces, retimes, or overwrites its member detections, and it is not an extractor output.

many_to_many.reason: A single interval over a many-to-many group would assert a correspondence the evidence does not support. The match group and its ambiguity topology remain the result.

unmatched.reason: A consensus event containing one extractor's detection alone would imply cross-extractor agreement that does not exist. Single-extractor evidence is carried by the unmatched match group and its consilience status.

feature_support.restrict_reason: Averaging two MUPET syllables to compare against one DeepSqueak call would require a scientific aggregation model that does not exist yet.

excluded_equivalence_classes.reason: registered as related with consilience_eligible = 0; power, energy, and amplitude are not interchangeable quantities

detection_agreement.denominator: that extractor's detection count within its own input run for this analysis
prohibitions: a split group is never counted as two independent one-to-one matches
ICC is not a detection-agreement metric

feature_agreement.scope: eligible feature pairs on one_to_one groups only

icc.reason: Not required by the contract, and with synthetic demonstration data it would characterise the fixture rather than extractor agreement.

statuses.rule: match_type = one_to_one with no eligible feature pair available
match_type = one_to_one and every eligible feature pair is within its declared tolerance
match_type = one_to_one and at least one eligible feature pair exceeds its declared tolerance
an independent manual review targets this group or its consensus event

consilience.semantics: A consilience status is an assessment derived from stated evidence under this versioned specification. It is not a probability that a vocalization occurred, and it must not be reported as one.

support_rule.supporting_comparisons_are: eligible feature pairs with a declared relative tolerance, excluding the timing classes reserved as primary temporal evidence
support_rule.missing_feature_effect: a comparison that could not be computed neither supports nor contradicts; it only reduces the count of available supporting comparisons

precedence.manual_status_storage: manual_reviews rows joined to the same match group; the automated status in consilience_assessments.status is never overwritten

manual_qc.independence: Manual review is independent evidence and is never derived from extractor state.

reference_events.coverage_meaning: the reviewer annotated the whole recording, so a detection with no overlapping reference event is a reviewed disagreement rather than an unreviewed region
reference_events.not_derived_from: any extractor detection, curation state, label, or score

matching_rule.purpose: detection to manual reference; deliberately separate from the extractor-to-extractor rule so one cannot be tuned through the other
matching_rule.assignment: greatest temporal IoU, each reference event and each detection used at most once

sensitivity.purpose: Demonstrate how results move with an uncalibrated threshold rather than to select a best value.
sensitivity.reporting_rule: state how outcomes move with the threshold; never label one configuration optimal, validated, or calibrated on synthetic data

components: this specification's profile key, version label, and checksum
analysis_identity.changed_spec_behavior: A changed specification, threshold, or algorithm version produces a new analysis run under a new run_key. An existing analysis is never rewritten in place.
analysis_identity.rerun_behavior: A rerun under the same run_key with identical inputs and an identical specification checksum reuses the existing analysis. Any difference in inputs or checksum is an explicit conflict.

upstream_immutability.statement: Matching consumes these rows and never writes, updates, or deletes any of them.
